input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: No audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right runs against Client anywhere in the Agreement, and TrueLink has no right of access to Client systems for usage verification. This was confirmed by exhaustive searching ("audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor", "books", "usage", "premises", "examination", "certif" — all nil or irrelevant) and by reading the sections where such a right would sit: Compensation (§ 5–6), Client covenants (§ 8) and Confidentiality (§ 10). The only information-flow rights point our way: § 6 entitles us to documentation supporting charges and to contest them, and § 2.e gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files. Because no audit obligation binds us, our position is better than the playbook's preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so there is no negotiation issue and no redline: proposing audit machinery would only create a vendor right that does not exist today. The failed deterministic check on "audit frequency limited" is explained by the total absence of an audit clause, not by a permissive one. Noted for awareness only (not a deviation under this rule): § 8.f lets TrueLink implement technical mechanisms to prevent spamming, but that operates on TrueLink's own Interface and is an acceptable-use enforcement measure, not an audit of our records or systems.
